target_customer: Startups and tech companies hiring engineering and product roles
problem: Hiring managers struggle to find qualified candidates who do not match listed keywords, and sourcing is manual and slow.
business_model: B2B recruiting service, AI sourcing with outreach, priced per engagement

founders.name: Kanjun Qiu
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as Founder/CEO and later CEO of Imbue. Education and prior employers not found in a source I opened.

founders.name: Josh Albrecht
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no bio.

competitors.name: Headstart
competitors.what: Candidate analysis and matching with deeper candidate-side involvement

competitors.name: Entelo
competitors.what: Recruiting software that announced Envoy, an AI feature delivering interested candidates
competitors.traction_then: More than 75 customers used Envoy in beta per a later release

technical_complexity.rationale: Building per-role ML models over public sources such as GitHub, papers and Stack Overflow is standard ML engineering with hard personalization parts, per the 2017 TechCrunch description.

defensibility.rationale: Models refine with each hire, but the sources are public and recruiting platforms could build similar sourcing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: LinkedIn and Indeed already had sourcing tools in 2017 and Entelo launched Envoy in October 2017. No source found on a later copy or purchase of Sourceress.

market_need_then: Engineering hiring was competitive in 2017 and recruiters spent time on manual sourcing. TechCrunch 2017 described the product as a way to find candidates managers want without realizing it.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found in my searches, only funding and founder coverage. The name is distinctive but no source shows it drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Sourceress raised a 3.5 million dollar round in November 2017 from Lightspeed, YC and angels, then stayed small relative to its AI-recruiting peers. The YC directory still lists it as Active with 35 people, while co-founder Kanjun Qiu went on to lead Imbue. No source found states why or when she moved on or what the company's trajectory was, so the outcome is unclear.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503 at fetch time. Aggregators (Seedtable, StartupIntros, Wellfound) label the round seed and one says $4M; TechCrunch states $3.5M without a stage label, so stage is other. Founding year 2015 appears on Seedtable only, so 2017 from the YC page is used. Outcome search found no acquisition or shutdown. Competitors are limited to ones named in TechCrunch 2017-11 and Entelo's 2017-10 launch.
